Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 14, "heading": "CHAPTER 12. LIKING LIFE ON MY OWN ACCOUNT NO BETTER, I FORM A GREAT RESOLUTION", "previous_rows": [], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 12, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u014-h", "tag": "h2", "role": "heading", "text": "CHAPTER 12. LIKING LIFE ON MY OWN ACCOUNT NO BETTER, I FORM A GREAT RESOLUTION", "sha256": "f6b0c6908522337e75399104a2162f6b1cb700546f357907948c3bf6339e0c03", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/h2", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": []}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0001", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "In due time, Mr. Micawber’s petition was ripe for hearing; and that gentleman was ordered to be discharged under the Act, to my great joy. His creditors were not implacable; and Mrs. Micawber informed me that even the revengeful boot-maker had declared in open court that he bore him no malice, but that when money was owing to him he liked to be paid. He said he thought it was human nature.", "sha256": "5f7fef6045511e23a89cd46ab77f8765f7867fcb52211b5fee54079e14b45137", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[1]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0002", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber returned to the King’s Bench when his case was over, as some fees were to be settled, and some formalities observed, before he could be actually released. The club received him with transport, and held an harmonic meeting that evening in his honour; while Mrs. Micawber and I had a lamb’s fry in private, surrounded by the sleeping family.", "sha256": "a15a36b73e196793d010ac00e4342aa3f8c074e0618af8515ee3f804a9c8594d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[2]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0003", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘On such an occasion I will give you, Master Copperfield,’ said Mrs. Micawber, ‘in a little more flip,’ for we had been having some already, ‘the memory of my papa and mama.’", "sha256": "64252a07bdbfd1aa7ec482c16f597fbf48fbba73095aba20fb0909c4c2bdec72", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[3]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0004", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Are they dead, ma’am?’ I inquired, after drinking the toast in a wine-glass.", "sha256": "cd0c21064d1b6d09093d9dcf0d6b30b9a91e699e4828c9ce493e00d6364bc704", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[4]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0005", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My mama departed this life,’ said Mrs. Micawber, ‘before Mr. Micawber’s difficulties commenced, or at least before they became pressing. My papa lived to bail Mr. Micawber several times, and then expired, regretted by a numerous circle.’", "sha256": "2f477853bb2092d115e6315aaf251bb45f66f22444ed9b9bc5ba4c86f2d642c6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[5]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0006", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mrs. Micawber shook her head, and dropped a pious tear upon the twin who happened to be in hand.", "sha256": "c17f79be08f681806bcc1dc21996aa2cffda70b05b22b178a31687629727cda7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[6]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0007", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "As I could hardly hope for a more favourable opportunity of putting a question in which I had a near interest, I said to Mrs. Micawber:", "sha256": "f9c2d51a3808118fd961da17e5ad410ec57db8cb308d9087d8c4bd24213a098f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[7]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0008", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘May I ask, ma’am, what you and Mr. Micawber intend to do, now that Mr. Micawber is out of his difficulties, and at liberty? Have you settled yet?’", "sha256": "fd4f2c5242c2d8e300cd369efade091119a4af86ac9b477f5705332cb74cc9d5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[8]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0009", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My family,’ said Mrs. Micawber, who always said those two words with an air, though I never could discover who came under the denomination, ‘my family are of opinion that Mr. Micawber should quit London, and exert his talents in the country. Mr. Micawber is a man of great talent, Master Copperfield.’", "sha256": "e6cbea01639e27c5268f32800e9318aaf65987e99d41e980cf69fc3438d1e639", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[9]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0010", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I said I was sure of that.", "sha256": "84cb4472943b2c485655da4a7babcd745df396774f388bd11ebbebf5fd27ff5f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[10]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0011", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Of great talent,’ repeated Mrs. Micawber. ‘My family are of opinion, that, with a little interest, something might be done for a man of his ability in the Custom House. The influence of my family being local, it is their wish that Mr. Micawber should go down to Plymouth. They think it indispensable that he should be upon the spot.’", "sha256": "b4d6a9a1de890118c7390167f8ddce6f999b4a093fe569a83dbca62794a89085", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[11]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0012", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘That he may be ready?’ I suggested.", "sha256": "9dd2e0e903f120f4c9f1e92478e0d8ce2bf92132df2198b958a042ef00d5b551", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[12]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0013", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Exactly,’ returned Mrs. Micawber. ‘That he may be ready—in case of anything turning up.’", "sha256": "938bec861902db65d7eaaf44f516fa1294c4fe40c18e345096869aab9912cc72", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[13]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0014", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And do you go too, ma’am?’", "sha256": "6aaaba38d3ee995758fc820ac1c95d01ab4a366e5567db93db80776ed91c2cdb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[14]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0015", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The events of the day, in combination with the twins, if not with the flip, had made Mrs. Micawber hysterical, and she shed tears as she replied:", "sha256": "200acdcf2533bb755d2b28564ed2efa0091bd3c3ef0d4fa5694c71e0c544f807", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[15]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0016", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I never will desert Mr. Micawber. Mr. Micawber may have concealed his difficulties from me in the first instance, but his sanguine temper may have led him to expect that he would overcome them. The pearl necklace and bracelets which I inherited from mama, have been disposed of for less than half their value; and the set of coral, which was the wedding gift of my papa, has been actually thrown away for nothing. But I never will desert Mr. Micawber. No!’ cried Mrs. Micawber, more affected than before, ‘I never will do it! It’s of no use asking me!’", "sha256": "605cd4665aca0373cb7e8347c5cb7e52da50456ca18880d7c57cc2be26f64873", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[16]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0017", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I felt quite uncomfortable—as if Mrs. Micawber supposed I had asked her to do anything of the sort!—and sat looking at her in alarm.", "sha256": "7fc2c24a7f0f9acde96e164847e94cc2081c34b8d238b1b30ee720624dcd74f8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[17]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0018", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Micawber has his faults. I do not deny that he is improvident. I do not deny that he has kept me in the dark as to his resources and his liabilities both,’ she went on, looking at the wall; ‘but I never will desert Mr. Micawber!’", "sha256": "efcd9e08ba1666f4917327529d3325e9435b5af0aa5cadaede28e3865738ec56", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[18]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0019", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mrs. Micawber having now raised her voice into a perfect scream, I was so frightened that I ran off to the club-room, and disturbed Mr. Micawber in the act of presiding at a long table, and leading the chorus of", "sha256": "37900df87ff70f51950cb99056d6d2d1f2a175bce9502c29cc6dc177ba79403e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[19]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0020", "tag": "p", "role": "verse_group", "text": "Gee up, Dobbin,
Gee ho, Dobbin,
Gee up, Dobbin,
Gee up, and gee ho—o—o!", "sha256": "0695db2a36b9ff32f0f5ab97bd734ffc06f0c64139fe732044d18dc5bafd016c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[20]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_lines": ["Gee up, Dobbin,", "Gee ho, Dobbin,", "Gee up, Dobbin,", "Gee up, and gee ho—o—o!"], "source_class": "poem"}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0021", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "—with the tidings that Mrs. Micawber was in an alarming state, upon which he immediately burst into tears, and came away with me with his waistcoat full of the heads and tails of shrimps, of which he had been partaking.", "sha256": "21897b2c0bca6b5baaa2b98e3587c12175f7d9e70a87b92511bcef65b14f900a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[21]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": "noindent"}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0022", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Emma, my angel!’ cried Mr. Micawber, running into the room; ‘what is the matter?’", "sha256": "1ebde94ebfa18f5769ab08357c0b5f233b272dc314d4cd77d5c11d31734017a2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[22]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0023", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I never will desert you, Micawber!’ she exclaimed.", "sha256": "12f01360f0ca2a106d81f1326264316b9839a16292e414fcd339bb07f5b82c57", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[23]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0024", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My life!’ said Mr. Micawber, taking her in his arms. ‘I am perfectly aware of it.’", "sha256": "aa5d9a3159ef4f754cf4c4ec4dcb991e9f9bb6001a1d6c4cc658b6b6279beecb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[24]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0025", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘He is the parent of my children! He is the father of my twins! He is the husband of my affections,’ cried Mrs. Micawber, struggling; ‘and I ne—ver—will—desert Mr. Micawber!’", "sha256": "2a61273277634c0735d336d49af219242be300ae721359f7c98f0b78bfc3046c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[25]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0026", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber was so deeply affected by this proof of her devotion (as to me, I was dissolved in tears), that he hung over her in a passionate manner, imploring her to look up, and to be calm. But the more he asked Mrs. Micawber to look up, the more she fixed her eyes on nothing; and the more he asked her to compose herself, the more she wouldn’t. Consequently Mr. Micawber was soon so overcome, that he mingled his tears with hers and mine; until he begged me to do him the favour of taking a chair on the staircase, while he got her into bed. I would have taken my leave for the night, but he would not hear of my doing that until the strangers’ bell should ring. So I sat at the staircase window, until he came out with another chair and joined me.", "sha256": "4fb67ae525bc064cbf20f41668ca63dbe18fe527f640cad3d98cccb58497fee6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[26]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0027", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘How is Mrs. Micawber now, sir?’ I said.", "sha256": "a61f78388f5037be90044c2ef79ea3851202602a27c26f50d860a719f4178c8b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[27]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0028", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Very low,’ said Mr. Micawber, shaking his head; ‘reaction. Ah, this has been a dreadful day! We stand alone now—everything is gone from us!’", "sha256": "dee6dcfca76b589dede4c61df4784e160043741de48186560ec2151ccd429afd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[28]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0029", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber pressed my hand, and groaned, and afterwards shed tears. I was greatly touched, and disappointed too, for I had expected that we should be quite gay on this happy and long-looked-for occasion. But Mr. and Mrs. Micawber were so used to their old difficulties, I think, that they felt quite shipwrecked when they came to consider that they were released from them. All their elasticity was departed, and I never saw them half so wretched as on this night; insomuch that when the bell rang, and Mr. Micawber walked with me to the lodge, and parted from me there with a blessing, I felt quite afraid to leave him by himself, he was so profoundly miserable.", "sha256": "750e4dd7de25c4953738478ff23b1cb11f43b52ead6026d93f92995a1628a6c6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[29]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0030", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But through all the confusion and lowness of spirits in which we had been, so unexpectedly to me, involved, I plainly discerned that Mr. and Mrs. Micawber and their family were going away from London, and that a parting between us was near at hand. It was in my walk home that night, and in the sleepless hours which followed when I lay in bed, that the thought first occurred to me—though I don’t know how it came into my head—which afterwards shaped itself into a settled resolution.", "sha256": "20e893594170252914fd9950af943caa1d0ad034ca1d6e93e798091c11ba5ecb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[30]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u014-b0031", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I had grown to be so accustomed to the Micawbers, and had been so intimate with them in their distresses, and was so utterly friendless without them, that the prospect of being thrown upon some new shift for a lodging, and going once more among unknown people, was like being that moment turned adrift into my present life, with such a knowledge of it ready made as experience had given me. All the sensitive feelings it wounded so cruelly, all the shame and misery it kept alive within my breast, became more poignant as I thought of this; and I determined that the life was unendurable.", "sha256": "b6e6e8dc417ff8227164b0dcc006913e5cb18c88bd5d313a076a4d7350d5b8e0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[19]/p[31]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
